preamble: Insertion of a glottal stop [ʔ] is a common way to give a vowel-initial syllable an onset or to break up vowel hiatus. Standard German inserts [ʔ] before vowel-initial stems in careful speech, and Indonesian inserts it at prefix-stem and stem-suffix boundaries where two vowels would otherwise meet. The inserted stop is usually predictable and unwritten.

examples.note: In careful speech a glottal stop occurs before word stems beginning with a vowel; it is more frequent in northern varieties and not usually treated as a phoneme.
A glottal stop is epenthesized to avoid vowel hiatus at the prefix-stem boundary; it is not written.
Inserted when a stem ending in /a/ takes the suffix -an; likewise bacaan [ba.t͡ʃa.ʔan] 'reading'.

sources: Wikipedia contributors. Standard German phonology: Consonants. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_German_phonology
